sections.section: Section 4 — Data Flow & Interaction Edge Cases
sections.summary: The compliance spine itself (append-only triggers, hash chain, ST_DWithin geofence math, idempotent-replay skeleton) is sound, but the interaction layer above it is where the plan is thinnest: the flagship keep-both conflict flow has no specified detection mechanism for its most common case (concurrent draft saves), finalized records can accrue silent edit-versions at the database layer because the form_version insert policy carries no status predicate, and the open-shift offer path both lacks its data model and omits the credential guard that the plan's "by construction" claim depends on. Tracing the six charter flows with shadow paths produced 13 findings (3 CRITICAL, 9 WARNING, 1 NOTE); all are fixable as spec/DDL-level changes if landed before the sprint that builds the affected surface (S2 forms, S4 scheduling, S6 EVV, S7 migration under the resequence).

findings.title: Draft-save concurrency has no specified detection mechanism — the flagship keep-both flow cannot fire for its most common case
findings.detail: Doc 08 §2 defines conflict detection as 'writes carry row_version; mismatch → 409 + CAREOS_CONFLICT_KEEP_BOTH' — an UPDATE-shaped mechanism on mutable rows. But form drafts are INSERTs into append-only form_version, granted directly to authenticated (Doc 07 §5: 'grant select, insert on public.form_version to authenticated'), with no save_draft RPC anywhere in the Doc 08 §3 catalog. An INSERT cannot carry a row_version compare-and-swap. Nothing enforces that a new version's prev_version_id equals the current head, and version_no assignment is unspecified: if client-computed (max+1), two devices collide on unique(instance_id,version_no) and get a raw unique-violation — not the keep-both flow; if server-assigned, both inserts succeed silently and the history becomes a fork (two children of the same parent) that the UI, which renders a chain, never surfaces. form_instance.current_version_id is described as 'convenience pointer (trigger-set)' — so the pointer becomes last-writer-wins across the fork. Downstream, an RN can review, sign, and finalize one fork while the other device's answers sit invisible in the losing branch: exactly the silent-divergence failure (pain #1 / principle P2) the product exists to eliminate. ST-023's AC ('simulated concurrent edit → 409 → side-by-side merge') asserts the behavior but no binding doc specifies a mechanism that can produce it.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §5 (form_version DDL: unique(instance_id,version_no), prev_version_id, insert grant, form_version_insert policy; form_instance.current_version_id comment); Doc 08 §2 (concurrency contract), §3 (RPC catalog — no draft-save RPC); Doc 10 §4 (conflict keep-both UX); Doc 15 ST-023; CLAUDE.md invariant 11
findings.recommendation: Add app.save_draft(p_instance, p_prev_version, p_content) to the Doc 08 §3 catalog and Doc 07 §5 DDL: server-assigns version_no under a form_instance row lock, asserts p_prev_version = current head, and on mismatch raises CAREOS_CONFLICT_KEEP_BOTH returning the head version id (the '409 + server copy' payload). Revoke the direct INSERT grant on form_version from authenticated (RPC-only writes, mirroring how finalize is the only path to 'final'). Resolve the current_version_id ownership contradiction (trigger-set per §5 comment vs RPC-set in finalize_form) to a single owner. Add a pgTAP case: two concurrent save_draft calls with the same prev → exactly one succeeds, one raises the conflict code. Land in Doc 07/08 before S2.

findings.title: Nothing at the DB layer stops edit-versions landing on a finalized instance (autosave racing finalize, browser-back, second device) — and finalize itself is re-runnable against a stale version
findings.detail: form_version_insert policy checks only tenant + AAL2 + author (Doc 07 §5) — no predicate on the parent instance's status. finalize_form takes FOR UPDATE on form_instance, but a debounced autosave (3 s, Doc 10 §4), a browser-back to a cached editor, or a second device that never saw the finalize will INSERT a kind='edit' version into a status='final' instance and succeed: the insert never touches the locked row. Doc 10 §4's 'post-sign state is visibly locked' is app-layer only, and Doc 06 §2 / CLAUDE.md invariant 2 explicitly rank app-layer enforcement as 'convenience' — the perimeter is Postgres, and the perimeter has no rule here. Worse, if current_version_id is trigger-set on version insert (§5 comment), the stray autosave repoints a signed, finalized record's current pointer at an unsigned draft. Separately, finalize_form never checks fi.status: a second finalize call with a stale/older version id (double-submit from a back-navigated review screen) silently repoints current_version_id backwards on an already-final instance — no CAREOS_ALREADY_FINAL guard, no idempotency contract.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §5 (form_version_insert policy — no status predicate; app.finalize_form body — no status guard, non-idempotent); Doc 10 §4 (autosave debounce; post-final lock is UI copy); Doc 08 §3 (correct_form is supposed to be the only post-final path); CLAUDE.md invariants 1–2
findings.recommendation: Add a DB guard (trigger or policy predicate) on form_version insert: when the parent instance is 'final'/'void', only kind='correction' via app.correct_form is accepted; edits raise a new catalog code CAREOS_FINALIZED. Harden finalize_form: raise CAREOS_ALREADY_FINAL if status='final' and p_version differs from current_version_id; no-op success if identical (idempotent replay). Mobile/web spec note in Doc 10 §4: on CAREOS_FINALIZED, the client converts pending local edits into a correction proposal draft rather than dropping them. pgTAP cases for both. Land before S2.

findings.title: accept_offer omits assert_schedulable — a credential lapsing between offer and accept schedules a non-compliant caregiver, breaking the plan's own 'by construction' guarantee
findings.detail: Doc 08 §3 is the binding RPC contract and its guard column is explicit per row: app.assign_shift lists 'schedule.write · assert_schedulable'; app.accept_offer lists only 'offeree'. An offer sent Tuesday and accepted Friday, with the caregiver's CPR/TB/license expiring Wednesday, therefore assigns a lapsed-credential caregiver through the accept path — the exact outcome Doc 07 §8 claims is impossible ('No worker ever serves a client with a lapsed license — by construction'). Doc 12 §3 only tests the assign path ('assert_schedulable blocks lapsed-credential assignment'), so the gap would also pass CI as specced. With a single human + agents building literally from the catalog (CLAUDE.md: 'you build from it, not around it'), the omission ships as written. COMAR 10.07.05.10/.11 credential requirements make this a citable compliance failure, not a UX bug. Note the same differential applies to the Coordination Agent's post-approval execution path (Doc 08 §7), which terminates in accept_offer.
findings.refs: Doc 08 §3 (guard column: assign_shift vs accept_offer rows), §7 (agent sequence ends in accept_offer); Doc 07 §8 (assert_schedulable contract + 'by construction' claim); Doc 12 §3 (pgTAP covers assign path only)
findings.recommendation: One-line catalog change: accept_offer guard = 'offeree · assert_schedulable (re-checked at accept time)', with a plain-language failure ('Your CPR certification expired Wednesday — this shift can't be confirmed; HR has been notified') and an automatic HR notification + offer re-open. Add the pgTAP case: offer → credential lapses → accept raises CAREOS_CREDENTIAL_BLOCK. Extend Doc 12 §3 wording to 'assert_schedulable blocks lapsed-credential assignment on every path that sets shift.caregiver_id'. Land before S4 (resequenced scheduling sprint).

findings.title: The offer entity does not exist in the binding schema — expiry, all-decline, mid-accept expiry, and the 'row lock' mechanism are all unspecifiable without it; SMS 'ACCEPT' has no lawful identity path
findings.detail: Doc 08 §3 defines offer_shift(shift, caregiver[]) and accept_offer(offer) with 'first-accept wins (row lock); rest expire' — but Doc 07 contains no shift_offer table: not in §6 DDL, not in the §10 data dictionary (checked every domain row). shift.status includes 'offered' but there is no row for accept_offer's offer argument to reference, no expires_at for 'offer expires mid-accept', no per-offeree decline state for 'all decline', and no answer to which row the lock takes. Consequences as specced: (a) all-offerees-decline has no terminal state — does the shift revert to 'open', re-plan via the agent, or page the coordinator? Unspecified. (b) Two accepts in the same millisecond are serializable only once the lock target exists; the loser needs a distinct code (CAREOS_OFFER_ALREADY_FILLED), not a generic failure. (c) The Doc 08 §7 sequence shows a Twilio 'ACCEPT' SMS reply invoking app.accept_offer — but the inbound webhook (Lane C) 'never holds service_role' (Doc 08 §1, CLAUDE.md invariant 6) and an SMS carries no user JWT, so there is no specified identity under which the RPC can lawfully run; phone-number→user binding and the execution mechanism are absent.
findings.refs: Doc 08 §3 (offer_shift/accept_offer rows), §7 (SMS ACCEPT sequence), §1 (Lane C service_role rule); Doc 07 §6 + §10 (no offer entity anywhere); Doc 15 ST-031a AC ('offer/accept RPC race-safe'); CLAUDE.md invariant 6
findings.recommendation: Add shift_offer DDL to Doc 07 §6: (id, tenant_id, shift_id, offeree_id, status offered|accepted|declined|expired|withdrawn, expires_at, responded_at, channel app|sms). Specify accept_offer semantics: SELECT shift FOR UPDATE → assert offer status='offered' AND now()<expires_at (expiry checked inside the lock) → assert_schedulable (S4-3) → assign; siblings → expired. Specify all-decline: shift back to 'open' + coordinator notification + optional agent re-plan (T1). For SMS accept, add a decision-log entry: either (a) SMS reply only deep-links to an authenticated in-app accept (no state change from the webhook), or (b) a narrowly-scoped Edge Function system job records an sms-channel acceptance pending in-app confirmation — pick one explicitly; option (a) is the invariant-clean default.

findings.title: Device-supplied p_at is completely unbounded — no future-time rejection, no skew flag, no shift-window bound, no clock_out ordering guard
findings.detail: app.clock_in accepts p_at (device time) and writes it into visit.clock_in_at and visit_event.at with zero validation (Doc 07 §6). visit_event.received_at exists but no rule ever compares them. So: a device with a wrong or deliberately altered clock can record an on-time clock-in hours late (p_at feeds the EVV begin/end elements submitted to ISAS and the EVV-verified billing gate, Doc 08 §6.1/§6.4 FR-AI-070); a future-dated p_at is accepted; a clock-in for a shift days in the past or future is accepted (the RPC checks caregiver ownership, never proximity to starts_at/ends_at). Legitimate offline sync arriving days late makes a naive freshness check wrong, so the bound must be conditional — which is exactly why it needs specifying rather than leaving to implementation. clock_out's body is not given at all, so clock_out-before-clock_in (cross-device replay ordering — PowerSync preserves per-device order, not cross-device order) and negative durations are unguarded.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §6 (app.clock_in body — p_at unvalidated; visit_event.at vs received_at; clock_out absent); Doc 08 §3 (clock_out listed, unspecified), §6.1 (Cures-Act time elements); Doc 10 §6 (offline capture doctrine)
findings.recommendation: Add an 'EVV time & ordering validation' block to Doc 07 §6, applied inside clock_in/clock_out: reject p_at > received_at + 5min (future times are always invalid, online or offline); when p_offline=false, |now() − p_at| > 10min → accept but flag exception kind 'time_anomaly'; p_at outside [shift.starts_at − 2h, shift.ends_at + 4h] → accept but flag exception (never block care, per the out-of-fence doctrine); clock_out requires an existing clock_in event for the visit or lands as an exception-flagged event, and clock_out_at < clock_in_at → exception. Record received_at alongside at in the ISAS payload posture question set (D-Q16). pgTAP time-travel cases for each.

findings.title: Geofence verdict ignores GPS accuracy — a 500 m-accuracy fix inside the 150 m fence yields within_geofence=true, feeding the 'EVV-verified' billing gate with noise
findings.detail: clock_in computes v_in := ST_DWithin(client.geo, point, geofence_radius_m) and captures p_accuracy into clock_in_accuracy_m — but the accuracy value plays no part in the verdict (Doc 07 §6). The boundary-exact case is fine (ST_DWithin is inclusive and deterministic), but the charter's harder case — GPS accuracy worse than the geofence radius (basements, urban canyons: the plan's own target environment, Doc 10 §1 'in a basement') — produces two failure shapes: false confidence (accuracy 500 m, point happens to land in-fence → verified=true, later cited as integrity evidence and consumed by the FR-AI-070 EVV-verified-only billing gate) and false exception (caregiver at the door, 200 m accuracy scatter lands the point 160 m out → exception noise for the coordinator queue). Doc 10 §6 samples best-of-N and shows accuracy, but no maximum-acceptable-accuracy policy or accuracy-aware verdict exists anywhere.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §6 (clock_in: st_dwithin call; p_accuracy captured, unused in verdict); Doc 10 §6 (best-of-N sampling, accuracy shown); Doc 06 §6.3; Doc 08 §6.4 (FR-AI-070 EVV-verified billing gate)
findings.recommendation: Make the geofence verdict three-state in Doc 07 §6: in / out / indeterminate, where indeterminate = accuracy_m > max(geofence_radius_m, configured threshold). Indeterminate records the visit, flags a soft exception distinct from out-of-fence (different coordinator queue label and different weight in EVV-verified billing eligibility), and the mobile UI says so honestly ('GPS is imprecise here — clocked in, flagged for review'). Change within_geofence_in/out from boolean to text verdict (or add a companion column) before S6 builds on it. pgTAP fixtures: exact-boundary, in-fence-bad-accuracy, out-by-less-than-accuracy.

findings.title: Stale-assignment offline visits dead-end: a shift cancelled/reassigned while the caregiver is offline makes the queued clock_in fail forever ('not your shift') or succeed against a cancelled shift — and late-arriving events never reconcile the no-show alerts that already fired
findings.detail: clock_in's first guard is s.caregiver_id = auth.uid() (Doc 07 §6). Trace: caregiver goes offline holding the shift in local SQLite (Doc 10 §6); coordinator reassigns it; the caregiver — unaware — performs the visit and clocks in locally ('Clocked in 2:01 PM — will sync'); on reconnect the PowerSync queue replays the RPC, which raises 'not your shift'. Doc 10 §6's doctrine says 'failures surface retry, never silent drop' — but retry can never succeed, and the plan defines no terminal path, so legitimately-performed care documentation (visit note, tasks, EVV times) is stranded. The mirror case: the RPC never checks shift.status, so clock-in against a cancelled shift silently succeeds, creates a visit, and enqueues an ISAS submission for a cancelled shift. Third leg: while the device is offline the server sees nothing — the office no-show flow (Doc 10 §2 exceptions queue) fires, escalates, possibly dispatches a replacement; when the events land days later (charter: 'sync arriving days late'), nothing in the plan auto-resolves the now-false no-show exception or reconciles the duplicate-coverage billing state. Doc 08 §6.1's 24h/72h aging alerts watch evv_submission rows, which don't exist until the device syncs — an unsynced device is invisible to every alert in the plan.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §6 (clock_in guards: caregiver match, no status check); Doc 10 §6 (offline doctrine: 'failures surface retry, never silent drop'), §2 (exceptions queue); Doc 08 §6.1 (aging alerts are submission-row-scoped); Doc 12 §4 (airplane-mode suite doesn't cover reassignment-while-offline)
findings.recommendation: Specify the terminal-failure path: on 'not your shift'/cancelled-shift replay, the sync layer converts the payload into a manual_attested exception visit (method='manual_attested', status='exception') bound to the original shift for coordinator adjudication — care documentation is never stranded. clock_in accepts cancelled-shift clock-ins but flags exception instead of silently succeeding. Late-arriving visit_events auto-resolve a matching open no-show exception (and re-open the billing determination) — add to app.review_visit_exception semantics. Add device-level sync-staleness monitoring (last-sync heartbeat per active caregiver device; alert when a caregiver with shifts today hasn't synced in N hours) to Doc 13's watch list. Add 'shift reassigned while offline' to the Doc 12 §4 airplane-mode E2E suite.

findings.title: A merge has two parents but form_version has one prev_version_id — ST-023's lineage AC is unimplementable as schemed — and the conflict-against-a-FINALIZED-version branch is unspecified
findings.detail: Doc 10 §4 promises 'outcome saved as a new version; both antecedents preserved and linked', and ST-023's AC demands a pgTAP lineage check proving it. But form_version carries a single prev_version_id (Doc 07 §5) and kind has no 'merge' value — the second antecedent is unrepresentable, so the lineage check cannot pass for a true merge. Two deeper shadow paths: (a) conflict against a FINALIZED version — an offline editor's sync collides with an instance someone finalized meanwhile; the keep-both UI cannot offer 'merge into the record' because post-final writes are corrections-only (reason mandatory, form.correct or author permission per Doc 08 §3), and the offline author (a caregiver) may lack correction rights over an RN-finalized assessment — the plan defines neither the conversion (edits → correction proposal) nor the routing when permissions don't allow it. With office-web + offline-mobile both editing, this WILL occur. (b) A merge resolution is itself a version insert and can lose a race to a third writer — recursive conflict needs a stated loop (re-conflict without losing merge work), which falls out of the S4-1 head-check mechanism but must be stated so the UI preserves in-progress merge state.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §5 (single prev_version_id; kind enum lacks 'merge'); Doc 10 §4 (both-antecedents promise); Doc 15 ST-023 AC (pgTAP lineage check); Doc 08 §3 (correct_form permissions)
findings.recommendation: Add merged_from_version_id uuid (second parent) and kind value 'merge' to form_version in Doc 07 §5; ST-023's pgTAP lineage assertion checks both pointers. Specify the conflict-vs-final branch in Doc 10 §4 + Doc 08: keep-both output against a final instance becomes a correction (reason pre-populated 'merge of concurrent offline edit') when the resolver holds form.correct; otherwise it parks as a 'proposed correction' draft routed to the finalizing role's inbox — never dropped. State the merge-race loop explicitly: merge save goes through the same head-check RPC; on conflict, re-enter merge UI with prior picks preserved.

findings.title: Recurrence is one dangling column: recurrence_id references no table, and series-vs-instance edit semantics, past-instance protection, and DST anchoring are all unspecified
findings.detail: The entire recurrence model in the binding schema is shift.recurrence_id uuid — 'series pointer' (Doc 07 §6) with no FK target, no rule storage (RRULE or equivalent), no exception/detachment concept, and no RPC in the Doc 08 §3 catalog for series operations. ST-030's AC scope includes 'recurrence' in one word. Unanswered edge cases the charter requires: edit-this-instance then edit-series (does the series edit clobber the detached instance?); cancel-series with completed/in-progress past instances (history must be untouched — completed shifts have visits, EVV events, and billing hanging off them); reassign-one-instance within an assigned series; and the DST trap — a 'daily 9:00 AM' shift stored as timestamptz UTC drifts an hour at each DST boundary unless the series anchors to local wall-clock time and regenerates instances; Doc 12 §2 has DST property tests for cadence math but nothing for scheduling recurrence. Under the resequence this lands at S4, so the spec gap is near-term.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §6 (shift.recurrence_id — no FK, no table); Doc 08 §3 (no series RPCs); Doc 15 ST-030 AC ('recurrence'); design doc sprint table (scheduler at S4); Doc 12 §2 (DST tests cadence-only)
findings.recommendation: Add a shift_recurrence table to Doc 07 §6 (rule as RRULE text or structured fields, local_timezone, anchor local time, generate-ahead horizon, status) and materialized-instance semantics: instances generated N weeks ahead; instance edits set detached=true (series edits skip detached rows); series cancel affects only future non-started instances (past/in-progress immutable by construction). Add edit-scope RPCs (app.update_series / app.detach_instance) to the Doc 08 catalog with 'this shift only / this and future' as the sole UI options (no 'all including past'). Anchor recurrence to local wall-clock with explicit DST behavior, and extend the Doc 12 §2 property tests to shift generation across spring-forward/fall-back.

findings.title: Migration identity resolution: the stated disambiguation keys (name+DOB+address) are all identical for cohabiting twins, and nothing forces adjudication when two existing clients match at similar confidence
findings.detail: Doc 14 §3 matches on 'name+DOB fuzzy' with 'high confidence → one-click confirm queue', and Doc 14 §7's mitigation for identity collisions is 'DOB/address adjudication rules'. For the charter's twin case — elderly twin siblings served in the same household, a real home-care scenario — surname, DOB, and address are all shared, and fuzzy name matching over OCR'd scans ('E. Johnson') collapses even the first-name signal. The mitigation is therefore insufficient by its own keys, and the one-click confirm queue is precisely where a coordinator rubber-stamps the wrong sibling at speed (the queue's purpose is to make the easy 80% fast, per §3's throughput plan). The plan's no-auto-merge principle protects against machine merges but not against machine-suggested, human-one-clicked misfiles — a misfiled assessment on the wrong twin is both a clinical-record error and a PHI-disclosure risk once family portal scoping exists.
findings.refs: Doc 14 §3 (candidate match: name+DOB fuzzy; one-click confirm queue), §7 row 3 (mitigation: DOB/address rules), §4 (duplicate-client scan gate)
findings.recommendation: Add a forced-adjudication rule to Doc 14 §3: when ≥2 existing candidate clients score above the match threshold — or share DOB+surname regardless of score — the document is routed to the side-by-side adjudication queue and is ineligible for one-click confirm, categorically. Extend match keys with tie-breakers that differ for twins: exact first/middle name, sex, Medicaid ID (Vault-accessor comparison), phone. Extend the §4 duplicate-client scan gate to explicitly enumerate same-DOB+surname pairs for human review before any cohort goes live. Seed the Meadowbrook universe (Doc 12 §7) with a twin-pair persona so the pipeline is tested against it.

findings.title: Readmission is unrepresentable: client has single admitted_on/discharged_on columns, so a re-admitted client overwrites episode history on a mutable row and the on_admission cadence semantics become undefined
findings.detail: The charter's 'client both active and re-admitted' case hits a schema wall: public.client carries exactly one admitted_on and one discharged_on (Doc 07 §5). Re-admission after discharge (common in home care) forces overwriting admitted_on/discharged_on on a mutable row — operational loss of the prior episode's dates in a product whose thesis is that nothing of consequence is overwritten (audit_event deltas make it forensically recoverable, not operationally usable). Three consequences: (a) the cadence engine 'derives due dates from admissions, latest satisfied obligations' (Doc 07 §7) with trigger_kind='on_admission' — whether a 2024-satisfied initial-assessment obligation suppresses the 2026 readmission's new 48-hr/initial obligations is unspecified, and a wrong implementation is a citable COMAR deficiency (no initial assessment on readmission); (b) Doc 14 migration will ingest 6-year-retention documents spanning both episodes with nowhere to record which admission a 2022 plan-of-care belongs to; (c) the Doc 14 §4 scorecard ('every active client has: current assessment, plan of care') needs 'current' to mean current-episode, which the schema cannot express.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §5 (client.admitted_on/discharged_on — scalar), §7 (evaluate_compliance derivation, trigger_kind on_admission); Doc 08 §3 (start_discharge/complete_discharge RPCs imply episodes); Doc 14 §3–4 (episode attribution, scorecard 'current')
findings.recommendation: Add an admission_episode table (client_id, admitted_on, discharged_on, status, discharge_form_instance_id) to Doc 07 §5; client.status derives from the open episode; admitted_on/discharged_on become convenience mirrors of the latest episode or are dropped. Key on_admission cadence rules and 'latest satisfied obligation' lookups to episode_id so a readmission re-triggers initial/48-hr obligations by construction, with a pgTAP time-travel case (admit → discharge → readmit → assert fresh obligations). Doc 14 pipeline attributes migrated documents to episodes by date-range; scorecard 'current' scopes to the open episode. This is expand-only DDL — cheap now, a data migration later.

findings.title: A document can belong to only one client — shared-household consents and two-client incident records misfile under exactly one chart, and the migration rule for them is unspecified
findings.detail: public.document has scalar client_id/employee_id (Doc 07 §9) and the Doc 14 §3 classifier resolves 'which client/employee it likely belongs to' — singular. The charter case (one document belonging to two clients) is routine where an agency serves both members of a couple in one household: a joint consent, an incident report involving two clients, a household-level service agreement. As specced, the document lands on one chart; the other client's Doc 14 §4 scorecard reports the consent missing (spawning a remediation task chasing a document that exists), or worse, a surveyor asks for client B's consent and it is filed under client A. Duplicating the file isn't specified either: storage_path is unique and sha256 carries no dedupe rule at the document-row level, so whether two document rows may share one storage object — and what RLS scoping each copy gets — is undefined.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §9 (document DDL: scalar client_id, unique storage_path); Doc 14 §3 (singular classification target), §4 (scorecard completeness per client)
findings.recommendation: Pick and specify one rule in Doc 07 §9 + Doc 14 §3. Preferred: a document_subject link table (document_id, client_id|employee_id) with RLS mirroring each subject's chart policy, and the classifier allowed to emit multiple subjects (each above its own confidence). Cheaper fallback: an explicit duplication rule — one document row per subject, same sha256, distinct storage_path copies, cross-referenced in provenance. Either way, the scorecard counts a document for every linked subject, and the migration adjudication UI supports 'belongs to both'.

findings.title: Two small EVV semantics to pin down: idempotency pre-check isn't scoped to the visit (backup-restored devices can get a false 'clocked in'), and midnight-spanning visits need an ISAS date-semantics answer under D-Q16
findings.detail: (a) clock_in's replay check is 'if exists (select 1 from visit_event where client_event_id=p_client_event) then return v_visit' (Doc 07 §6) — unscoped to the visit or kind. client_event_id is globally unique, so accidental UUID collision is negligible, but the realistic path is a device backup/restore or phone migration duplicating the local queue onto two devices: the same client_event_id can then replay against a different shift, and the RPC returns the current shift's visit as success without recording anything — a silent false-success in the EVV path. (b) A visit spanning midnight (evening shift 10 PM–6 AM) has one clock-in date and a different clock-out date; whether ISAS expects a single record, a date-split, or service-date attribution is a state-modality question nothing in Doc 08 §6.1 or the D-Q16 question set currently asks; billing/board day-bucketing should also state which date owns the visit.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §6 (idempotency pre-check, unscoped); Doc 08 §6.1 (six elements; no overnight rule); Doc 00 V10 / design doc open question 6 (D-Q16 question set)
findings.recommendation: Scope the pre-check: 'where client_event_id=p_client_event and visit_id=v_visit.id then return'; an existing event under a different visit raises a conflict code (CAREOS_EVENT_ID_REUSED) so the device re-keys instead of believing a false success. Add overnight-visit record semantics (and late-submission window rules, which also serve S4-7) to the D-Q16 question list for the state/MCO contact, and state the service-date attribution rule for boards/billing (recommend: date of clock-in).

sections.section: S5 — Code Quality of the binding SQL (docs/07, with docs/08 RPC catalog cross-checks)
sections.summary: The spine's shape is right — the append-only pattern, idempotency keys (visit_event.client_event_id, ON CONFLICT (shift_id)), STABLE volatility on the RLS helpers, and the finalize_form signature-set EXCEPT logic all check out under adversarial tracing (v.template_id resolves via fi.*; the charter's suspected join-variable bug does not exist). But four defects are CRITICAL because downstream pgTAP tests will be generated from these same wrong expectations and will pass: the audit hash chain forks under ordinary concurrency and hashes non-deterministic text renderings; the entire e-signature evidence chain (content_hash) is comment-enforced, not constraint-enforced; the form_version INSERT policy permits cross-tenant appends into any instance; and finalize_form (SECURITY DEFINER) never checks tenant, status, or latest-version. Below that sit systematic completeness gaps — missing FKs including two unfulfilled "FK added later" promises, missing enable-RLS lines on a granted table, a client INSERT grant with no INSERT policy, an audit_anchor PK that breaks the day the Meadowbrook demo tenant (E3) exists, a missing clock_out spec, and standard-column/row_version convention violations on 9 tables — all cheap to fix in doc 07 now and expensive after migration 0001 is cut.

findings.title: audit.compute_chain forks under concurrency and hashes non-deterministic input — the tamper-evidence ledger can raise false tamper alarms
findings.detail: The BEFORE INSERT trigger reads the previous hash with `select hash ... where tenant_id = new.tenant_id order by id desc limit 1`. Under READ COMMITTED, two concurrent same-tenant transactions (guaranteed by invariant 7: every consequential action emits audit in-transaction) both read the same prev row, producing two events with identical prev_hash — a fork. A verifier walking the chain by id then finds row N+1 whose prev_hash != hash(row N) and reports tampering that never happened, permanently, in an append-only table that cannot be repaired. Second defect: the hash input includes `new.occurred_at::text` — timestamptz text rendering depends on the session's TimeZone/DateStyle GUCs (PostgREST sessions, pg_cron, a psql operator, and the future verification job can all differ), so even a clean chain may fail re-verification. Third (minor): the prev-hash lookup has no supporting index — idx_audit_entity is (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, id) and cannot serve `where tenant_id order by id desc`.
findings.refs: docs/07 §4: audit.compute_chain(), trg_audit_chain, idx_audit_entity; CLAUDE.md invariant 7
findings.recommendation: In compute_chain: (1) take `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('audit_'||new.tenant_id::text, 0))` as the first statement to serialize per-tenant chain writes; (2) make hash input GUC-independent — e.g. `to_char(new.occurred_at at time zone 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')` (record the exact canonical serialization rule in §4 so the verifier and the anchor-export job implement the same bytes); (3) add `create index idx_audit_tenant_seq on audit.audit_event (tenant_id, id desc)`. Add a pgTAP test that runs two concurrent inserts and asserts the chain verifies.

findings.title: The e-sign evidence chain (content_hash) is enforced by comments, not constraints — legal signature evidence can be silently wrong
findings.detail: Three links, all vibes: (1) form_version.content_hash is documented as `sha256(canonical(content))` but nothing computes or validates it — form_version has `grant insert to authenticated` (Lane-A draft saves), so the hash is client-supplied and can be arbitrary; no canonicalization function is specified anywhere. (2) signature.content_hash says `-- must equal version.content_hash` — a comment; no constraint or trigger enforces equality. (3) finalize_form selects fv.content_hash into v and then never uses it. Meanwhile docs/08 §5 legally leans on exactly this: 'signature row binds content_hash of the exact form_version (any content change = new version = new signature required)'. The only guard point, app.sign_version, exists solely as a one-line catalog row in docs/08 §3 — no DDL in the 'real DDL' doc, and the signature table has no grants or policies at all, so the signing path is unimplementable as specified.
findings.refs: docs/07 §5: form_version.content_hash, signature.content_hash, app.finalize_form; docs/08 §3 app.sign_version, §5 native e-sign (D-004)
findings.recommendation: Make the chain structural: (1) BEFORE INSERT trigger on form_version sets `new.content_hash := digest(new.content::text,'sha256')` — jsonb::text is deterministic (sorted, deduped keys), so declare `content::text` as the canonical form in §5 and forbid client-side hash computation; (2) `alter table form_version add constraint uq_fv_id_hash unique (id, content_hash);` then `alter table signature add constraint fk_sig_version_hash foreign key (form_version_id, content_hash) references form_version (id, content_hash)` — equality becomes a FK, unfalsifiable; (3) write app.sign_version DDL in §5 (asserts AAL2, signer_role ∈ template.requires_signature_roles, stamps session_aal from auth.jwt(), emits audit), and give signature a SELECT policy so signed evidence is renderable.

findings.title: form_version_insert policy allows any user to append versions to any instance — including other tenants' — and version_no is client-chosen
findings.detail: The INSERT policy checks only `tenant_id = app.current_tenant_id() and app.is_aal2() and author_id = auth.uid()`. instance_id is unconstrained: the FK requires only existence (FKs ignore RLS), so a tenant-A user can insert version rows stamped tenant_id=A onto a tenant-B form_instance. Victim can't see them (their SELECT policy filters tenant), but `unique (instance_id, version_no)` spans tenants, so the attacker's rows squat version numbers and block the victim's next save — corruption + DoS of an append-only PHI record with no repair path (AO trigger forbids DELETE). Within-tenant it's also wider than the read policy: no care-team/creator check, so any staff member can append to any instance they cannot even read. Separately, nothing assigns version_no — two devices saving concurrently pick the same number and one fails on the unique constraint with no keep-both flow at this layer (invariant 11).
findings.refs: docs/07 §5: policy form_version_insert, unique (instance_id, version_no), grant insert on form_version; CLAUDE.md invariants 2, 11
findings.recommendation: Extend WITH CHECK to bind the parent: `exists (select 1 from form_instance fi where fi.id = instance_id and fi.tenant_id = form_version.tenant_id and fi.status in ('draft','in_review') and (fi.created_by = auth.uid() or app.has_perm('form.write.all') or (fi.client_id is not null and app.on_care_team(fi.client_id))))`. Assign version_no server-side: BEFORE INSERT trigger that locks the instance row and sets max(version_no)+1 (or move draft saves to an app.save_form_version RPC and revoke the raw insert grant — decide and record which). Add the cross-tenant-append case to the pgTAP matrix explicitly.

findings.title: finalize_form (SECURITY DEFINER) has no tenant guard, no status precondition, and no latest-version check
findings.detail: The function verifies AAL2 and `has_perm('form.finalize') or v.created_by = auth.uid()` but never compares v.tenant_id to app.current_tenant_id(). has_perm is tenant-blind at check time, and SECURITY DEFINER (owner: Supabase `postgres`, which carries bypassrls) skips RLS — so any user holding form.finalize in their own tenant (e.g. the E3 Meadowbrook demo tenant) can finalize any instance in any tenant by UUID; the emit_audit call then stamps the attacker's tenant on the audit event, corrupting the victim tenant's evidence trail too. Additionally: no check of fi.status (a 'void' or already-'final' instance can be re-finalized), no check that p_version is the instance's latest version (finalizing an older version silently reverts content while pointing current_version_id at it), and docs/08 §3 promises finalize 'supersedes prior' but no supersede logic or superseded_by column exists — form_instance has a 'superseded' status with no writer. Traced-and-clean for the record: the signature EXCEPT check is correct, v.template_id resolves (fi.* includes it), and FOR UPDATE on the joined AO row is lock-only (no trigger fires).
findings.refs: docs/07 §5: app.finalize_form; docs/08 §3 row app.finalize_form ('supersedes prior'); docs/07 §5 form_instance.status, current_version_id '(trigger-set)' comment with no trigger defined
findings.recommendation: Add to finalize_form (and adopt as a mandatory preamble template for every SECURITY DEFINER RPC): `if v.tenant_id is distinct from app.current_tenant_id() then raise exception 'CAREOS_NOT_FOUND'; end if;` plus `if v.status not in ('draft','in_review') then raise` and `if v.version_no <> (select max(version_no) from form_version where instance_id = p_instance) then raise`. Either implement supersede (add form_instance.superseded_by uuid; finalize marks the prior final instance of the same (client, template key)) or delete the claim from docs/08 §3. Fix the stale '(trigger-set)' comment — the RPC sets the pointer.

findings.title: RLS enablement and policy/grant coverage is inconsistent in the binding DDL — form_version has grants + policies but no ENABLE/FORCE; client has an INSERT grant with no INSERT policy
findings.detail: Only `client` receives explicit `enable/force row level security` in the entire doc. `form_version` gets policies and `grant select, insert to authenticated` but no enable statement — Postgres happily creates policies on a non-RLS table and they are inert, so if migration 0001 is generated by copying §5 verbatim (the doc's own claim: '§3–9 are real DDL'), form_version is cross-tenant readable/writable by every authenticated user. Rated WARNING not CRITICAL only because convention §1.4 states the rule and a generic structural check can catch it mechanically — unlike S5-3/S5-4 whose wrong logic propagates into the generated tests. Second defect, explicitly a dead end: client has `grant select, insert, update` but only SELECT and UPDATE policies — with forced RLS, no INSERT policy means every insert is denied, and no client-creation RPC exists in the docs/08 §3 catalog either, so admission/intake has no specified write path at all. Third: app_user, form_instance, form_template, signature, shift, visit have neither grants nor policies in the binding DDL — fail-closed (fine if deferred to the §11 generated catalog), but form_instance CRUD and signature SELECT are spine-level and belong in §5.
findings.refs: docs/07 §5 lines: enable/force only on public.client; policy set {client_select_scoped, client_write_admin} vs `grant select, insert, update on public.client`; form_version grants/policies with no enable; §1 convention 4; §11; docs/08 §3 (no client-create RPC)
findings.recommendation: (1) Add `alter table ... enable row level security; force row level security;` beside every CREATE TABLE in §3–9. (2) Add a structural pgTAP canary — every table in schema public must have relrowsecurity AND relforcerowsecurity true — and wire it into the E4 spec-drift CI gate so this class can never ship. (3) Resolve the client INSERT path: either add `client_insert_admin` (WITH CHECK tenant + aal2 + client.write) or drop the insert grant and add app.create_client/app.admit_client to the docs/08 catalog — record which. (4) Add form_instance policies and signature SELECT policy to §5.

findings.title: app.current_tenant_id() is invoker-rights and reads app_user (no grant exists) — every scoped query errors; and no policy uses the wrap-in-select caching idiom
findings.detail: Helper volatility is correct (STABLE across the board — charter question answered), but the helpers are inconsistently privileged: has_perm/on_care_team are SECURITY DEFINER while current_tenant_id is not, yet it also reads a table. §2 revokes all on public from authenticated and app_user receives no grant/policy anywhere in the doc, so the first evaluation of client_select_scoped calls current_tenant_id() under the caller's rights and fails with 'permission denied for table app_user' — every Lane-A query on client breaks. Loud, but it proves the mixed helper styles are a bug generator. Performance: every policy invokes helpers bare — `app.has_perm('client.read.all')`, `app.is_aal2()`, `app.current_tenant_id()` — which Postgres evaluates per row; SECURITY DEFINER functions are never inlined, so a 5,000-row list view runs 15,000 catalog-joining function calls. The standard Supabase idiom — wrapping row-invariant calls as `(select app.has_perm('...'))` to get a once-per-statement InitPlan — is used nowhere. DRY: the `tenant_id = app.current_tenant_id() and app.is_aal2()` pair is hand-repeated in every policy with no canonical template, so one forgotten is_aal2 on one PHI table = silent MFA bypass across ~63 planned policies.
findings.refs: docs/07 §3.1: app.current_tenant_id, app.has_perm, app.on_care_team, app.is_aal2; §5 policies client_select_scoped, form_version_select/insert; §2 revoke-all; §11 (63 policies)
findings.recommendation: (1) Prefer deriving tenant_id from a custom JWT claim (Supabase custom access token hook) so current_tenant_id() is `(auth.jwt()->>'tenant_id')::uuid` — no table read, no definer needed; else make it SECURITY DEFINER with pinned search_path like its siblings. (2) Define one canonical policy template in §1 conventions — `(select app.current_tenant_id()) = tenant_id and (select app.is_aal2()) and (select app.has_perm('...')) or app.on_care_team(<row col>)` — row-invariant calls wrapped, row-dependent ones bare — and generate the 63 policies from it. (3) Add a pgTAP/canary assertion that every policy on a PHI-class table references is_aal2.

findings.title: Fourteen missing FK constraints, including two explicit 'FK added later' promises that are never fulfilled, and a dangling shift.recurrence_id with no recurrence table anywhere
findings.detail: The doc establishes the deferred-FK pattern correctly once (care_team_assignment.client_id → §5 ALTER fk_cta_client) then breaks its own promises: form_instance.employee_id says 'FK in §8' and form_instance.visit_id says 'FK in §6' — neither section adds them. compliance_obligation.employee_id, form_version.ai_interaction_id (ai.ai_interaction is dictionary-only), form_instance.current_version_id, credential.document_id (ordering: §8 precedes §9), document.uploaded_by, credential.verified_by, compliance_obligation.waived_by all lack FKs. tenant_id is FK'd on 8 tables and bare on 7 (visit_event, evv_submission, compliance_obligation, credential_type, credential, document, audit_anchor) with no stated rule for the difference. shift.recurrence_id ('series pointer') references nothing — no recurrence table exists in §3–9 or the §10 dictionary: a dangling design element. Bonus integrity gap: user_role has no congruence constraint between the user's tenant and the role's tenant, so a tenant-B role can be granted to a tenant-A user and has_perm returns true on it. Full enumeration in artifact Table A.
findings.refs: docs/07 §5 form_instance ('FK in §6', 'FK in §8' comments), §5 form_version.ai_interaction_id, §6 shift.recurrence_id + visit_event/evv_submission, §7 compliance_obligation, §8 credential/credential_type, §9 document, §3 user_role; contrast §5 alter table fk_cta_client
findings.recommendation: Add the ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT statements at the sections where the referenced tables exist (Table A gives the exact placement per column). Add `check ((kind = 'ai_draft') = (ai_interaction_id is not null))` on form_version. Either spec a shift_recurrence table or delete recurrence_id until it has a target. For tenant_id: state the rule (recommend: FK on every table except audit.* with a documented exemption). For user_role congruence: add unique(id, tenant_id) on app_user and role, then composite FKs from a tenant_id column on user_role. Add a CI drift check (E4 gate): every *_id column FKs something or carries a documented exemption comment.

findings.title: audit.audit_anchor PK is (day) alone — the daily WORM anchor export breaks the day a second tenant exists, which is day one (E3 Meadowbrook demo tenant)
findings.detail: `create table audit.audit_anchor (day date primary key, tenant_id uuid not null, ...)` permits exactly one tenant's anchor per calendar day. The accepted CEO expansion E3 stands up a Meadowbrook demo tenant alongside the production tenant, so from the first production day the anchor job's second insert violates the PK and one tenant's tamper-evidence root silently never reaches WORM storage — the exact evidence a surveyor asks for. Also: audit_anchor carries no forbid_mutation protection despite being the chain's exported root (exported_at legitimately updates, but day/root_hash/last_event_id must not).
findings.refs: docs/07 §4: audit.audit_anchor; CEO plan E3 (demo tenant); docs/07 §4 audit chain purpose
findings.recommendation: `primary key (tenant_id, day)`. Add a column-level guard trigger (allow UPDATE of exported_at only, forbid all else + DELETE). Add a pgTAP test inserting anchors for two tenants on the same day.

findings.title: clock_in: re-clock-in overwrites geofence evidence, no shift-status precondition, NULL-geo clients always become 'exception' — and clock_out, the billing-critical half, has no DDL at all
findings.detail: (a) The idempotency check keys on client_event_id only; a second clock-in with a fresh event id (second device, retap) passes it, and the UPDATE coalesces only clock_in_at while unconditionally overwriting clock_in_geo, accuracy, within_geofence_in, and status — the original geofence evidence on the visit row is replaced (the AO visit_event keeps both, but the derived row lies). (b) No check of shift.status: clocking into a 'cancelled' or 'completed' shift succeeds and force-flips it to in_progress via the unconditional shift UPDATE. (c) client.geo is nullable; st_dwithin(NULL,...) yields NULL, and `case when v_in then 'in_progress' else 'exception' end` sends every visit for a not-yet-geocoded client to 'exception' with within_geofence_in NULL — behavior by accident, not decision. (d) p_at/p_offline are trusted as claimed; visit_event.received_at exists (good) but nothing flags an online submission whose p_at is hours stale. (e) app.clock_out is a docs/08 §3 catalog row with zero DDL, yet it owns the hard parts: duration, visit completion, shift→completed, the EVV end-time element, and the same idempotency/replay discipline. §3–9 claims to be the real DDL where correctness is existential; the out-half of EVV qualifies.
findings.refs: docs/07 §6: app.clock_in (coalesce line, status case, shift update), public.client.geo nullable, visit_event.received_at; docs/08 §3 app.clock_in/app.clock_out row, §6.1 six Cures-Act elements
findings.recommendation: (a) After the FOR UPDATE, `if v_visit.clock_in_at is not null then return v_visit; end if;` (treat any second clock-in as replay). (b) Precondition `s.status in ('scheduled','in_progress')` else raise CAREOS_* code. (c) Decide NULL-geo semantics explicitly (recommend: within_geofence_in NULL + status 'in_progress' + a 'geocode_missing' flag in the event payload, not 'exception'). (d) Record `extract(epoch from now()-p_at)` in visit_event.payload; auto-flag online submissions with delta > threshold. (e) Write app.clock_out DDL in §6 mirroring clock_in (idempotent via client_event_id, requires clock_in_at not null, sets shift completed, enqueues q_evv_isas with both times).

findings.title: Nine tables violate the binding standard-columns convention (created_at / updated_at / row_version on mutable tables) — and the promised updated_at trigger is never defined
findings.detail: Convention §1.3 is binding: every domain table gets created_at; mutable tables get updated_at via trigger + row_version. Violations (full matrix in artifact Table B): visit is mutated on every clock event yet has none of the three; care_team_assignment is mutated (ends_on set on unassignment — the security-relevant scoping table) with no updated_at/row_version; form_template has a mutable lifecycle (draft→active→retired) and none of the three; document's legal_hold/retention_until are consequential mutations with no updated_at/row_version; evv_submission and compliance_obligation lack created_at/row_version; employee, credential, credential_type lack created_at; tenant lacks updated_at. docs/08 §2 makes row_version the concurrency contract ('writes carry row_version; mismatch → 409 CAREOS_CONFLICT_KEEP_BOTH') — impossible on these tables as declared. Finally, 'updated_at via trigger' names a trigger that appears nowhere in §3–9 (no app.touch_updated_at()), and finalize_form/clock_in instead set updated_at manually — two patterns for one promise.
findings.refs: docs/07 §1 convention 3; §6 visit, evv_submission; §3 care_team_assignment, tenant; §5 form_template; §7 compliance_obligation; §8 employee, credential, credential_type; §9 document; docs/08 §2 concurrency
findings.recommendation: Add the missing columns per Table B. Define app.touch_updated_at() once in §3.1 and attach it to every mutable table; delete the manual updated_at assignments from RPCs. For tables that are deliberately RPC-only (visit, evv_submission, compliance_obligation), amend convention 3 with an explicit 'RPC-mutated: row_version exempt' clause so the exemption is a decision, not an accident — and add an E4 drift check asserting column conformance for everything else.

findings.title: app.emit_audit cannot record system actions — cron/worker contexts have auth.uid() NULL, so tenant_id resolves NULL and the insert violates NOT NULL
findings.detail: emit_audit derives tenant via app.current_tenant_id() (a lookup on auth.uid()). The cadence engine app.evaluate_compliance runs under pg_cron (§7, careos_cadence_tick) and app.submit_evv runs as a worker (docs/08 §3 'system') — both have no auth context, so current_tenant_id() returns NULL and the audit insert fails on audit_event.tenant_id NOT NULL. Yet audit_event.actor_id is explicitly nullable ('null = system') and actor_kind has 'system'/'agent' values — the schema anticipates system events that the only emit function cannot produce. Invariant 7 (every consequential action emits audit) is unimplementable for exactly the automated half of the platform.
findings.refs: docs/07 §4: app.emit_audit, audit_event.tenant_id not null / actor_id nullable / actor_kind; §7 cron.schedule careos_cadence_tick; docs/08 §3 app.submit_evv (system)
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit-tenant overload `app.emit_audit(p_tenant uuid, p_action text, ...)` for system contexts (EXECUTE granted only to internal roles), keep the current signature delegating to it via current_tenant_id() with a `raise if null` guard so a NULL tenant fails loudly with a CAREOS_* code instead of a constraint error. Set actor_kind from context ('system' when auth.uid() is null).

findings.title: Consistency nits: RPCs use `select *` (banned by the constitution), policy names drop the <who> segment, and three enum-ish text columns lack CHECKs
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md ('You never... use select * in policies/RPCs') is violated by the binding DDL itself: clock_in uses `select * into v_visit` and `select c.* into v_client`; finalize_form uses `fi.*`. Naming convention §1.7 mandates policies `<table>_<action>_<who>`: form_version_select and form_version_insert lack the <who> segment; client_write_admin uses 'write' for an UPDATE-only policy. Enum-as-text CHECK coverage is otherwise consistent (verified across all 20 CHECKed columns) except: evv_submission.target (default 'isas', unchecked), signature.session_aal (should be constrained to 'aal2' — it is AAL2 evidence), and signature.signer_role (free text matched by string equality against requires_signature_roles in finalize — a typo'd role blocks finalize with no earlier validation point). None of these is a runtime defect today; all are exactly the drift the E4 gate exists to catch, and the constitution-vs-spec contradiction on select * will confuse coding agents on day one.
findings.refs: CLAUDE.md 'You never' list; docs/07 §1 conventions 6-7; §5 app.finalize_form, policies form_version_select/insert, client_write_admin, signature.session_aal/signer_role; §6 app.clock_in, evv_submission.target
findings.recommendation: Replace star-selects with explicit column lists in both RPCs (or amend the constitution rule to permit whole-row record fetch in plpgsql, and say so). Rename policies to convention (form_version_select_scoped, form_version_insert_author, client_update_admin). Add CHECKs: evv_submission.target in ('isas'), signature.session_aal in ('aal2'); validate signer_role against the template's role set inside app.sign_version (per S5-2).

sections.summary: Doc 12 is a genuinely strong strategy for the things it names — the pgTAP RLS matrix with a build-failing coverage manifest, the airplane-mode suite, the planted-PHI canary, and the AI eval gates are better than incumbent practice. But it has a structural blind spot: the pyramid contains no layer capable of testing concurrency, and three of the product's core guarantees (audit-chain linearity, accept_offer first-wins, keep-both under simultaneous save) are concurrency properties — worse, the audit-chain trigger as written in Doc 07 §4 will actually fork under normal concurrent load, producing false tamper pages, and only a concurrency test can catch it. The second structural gap: PowerSync sync rules are the sole read-authorization for mobile (logical replication bypasses RLS) yet get no named test layer or coverage gate while RLS gets ~700 assertions. Finally, the five accepted expansions (E1/E3/E4/E5/E6) post-date Doc 12 and currently have zero named tests, and several evidence-producing features (survey packet, migration scorecard) are tested as journeys but never against a COMAR ground-truth oracle.

findings.title: No concurrency test layer exists anywhere in the pyramid — and the audit-chain trigger will fork under normal concurrent load
findings.detail: Doc 12 §2's pyramid is pgTAP (single-session), Vitest/supertest, Playwright, Maestro, k6 — none can drive two simultaneous database transactions and assert the interleaving outcome. Yet three headline guarantees are concurrency properties: (1) audit-chain linearity — audit.compute_chain() (Doc 07 §4) reads the chain head with an unlocked SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 in a BEFORE INSERT trigger; under READ COMMITTED, two concurrent same-tenant inserts both read the same head and both write the same prev_hash, forking the chain. ACT is single-tenant and every consequential action calls app.emit_audit, so same-tenant concurrent inserts are the steady state (Doc 12 §2's own 'Mon 8am shift-start storm'). The daily chain-verify job (Doc 09 §7) then pages 'audit-chain verify failure' (Doc 13 §7 page condition) — a false tamper alarm from normal load; alternatively, if verification is written leniently enough to tolerate forks, real tampering becomes undetectable. Doc 12 §3's audit test ('Insert sequence → recompute hashes → assert linkage') is strictly sequential and cannot catch either failure. (2) app.accept_offer 'first-accept wins (row lock)' — ST-031's AC says 'race-safe... under concurrency test' but no layer, harness, or tool for that test exists in Doc 12. (3) keep-both under two simultaneous saves (see S6-3). A guarantee whose only threat model is concurrency, tested only sequentially, is untested.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §4 audit.compute_chain / trg_audit_chain / app.emit_audit; Doc 12 §2 (pyramid), §3 (audit chain test); Doc 08 §3 app.accept_offer; Doc 15 ST-031 AC; Doc 09 §7 chain-verify job; Doc 13 §7 page matrix
findings.recommendation: Two plan changes, both in the D-009 doc-delta list: (a) fix the design — serialize chain append per tenant (e.g., pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(tenant_id::text)) at the top of compute_chain, or a locked per-tenant chain-head row), and note the write-throughput implication for the k6 writes-p95<800ms budget since all audited writes per tenant now serialize; (b) add a named 'DB concurrency' layer to Doc 12 §2 — a multi-connection harness (Vitest with N parallel pg connections against the migrated ephemeral DB, or pgbench scripts) run in the same CI stage as pgTAP — with three named tests: parallel-insert chain linearity (assert exactly one child per hash after N concurrent emit_audit calls), accept_offer with N racers (exactly one 'scheduled', rest expired), and concurrent form_version save. Land it in S0 with ST-003, because the chain trigger ships in migration 0001–0004.

findings.title: PowerSync sync rules are the only read-authorization for mobile (replication bypasses RLS) but have no test layer, tooling, or coverage gate
findings.detail: Doc 08 §6.8: PowerSync reads come from logical replication 'filtered by sync rules that mirror care_team_assignment scoping.' Logical replication does not evaluate RLS — so for every table synced to devices, the hand-authored sync rules are the entire PHI read perimeter, exactly as authoritative as the RLS policies Doc 12 §3 covers with ~700 generated assertions and a build-failing coverage manifest ('adding a table without matrix coverage fails the build'). The sync-rule surface gets none of that: Doc 12 never mentions sync rules; ST-033's AC says 'verified against fixture matrix' but no layer, harness, or generator is defined anywhere; and nothing re-verifies when sync scope changes later (S6 adds EVV/visit/task tables to the synced set; Doc 13 §3 explicitly anticipates sync-rule evolution). This contradicts Doc 12 §1's own philosophy — 'least privilege... tested in the database, where enforced' — because mobile reads are not enforced in the database at all. An over-broad sync rule silently delivers another client's chart to a caregiver's phone: PHI exposure with no detecting control (the canary suite watches egress channels, not sync buckets).
findings.refs: Doc 08 §6.8; Doc 12 §1.1, §3 (RLS matrix + coverage manifest — sync rules absent); Doc 15 ST-033 AC; Doc 13 §3 (PowerSync compatibility rules), §6 (sync health = ops only); Doc 10 §6 (sync scope: 'their shifts ±14d, their clients' charts-lite')
findings.recommendation: Add to Doc 12 §3 a 'sync-rule matrix' sibling of the RLS matrix, landing with ST-033 at S5: generated tests over (user × assignment fixture × synced table) asserting exact bucket contents per device identity (tenant-B rows, off-team clients, ±14d window boundaries, post-revocation eviction), plus a coverage manifest so any table added to sync rules without matrix coverage fails the build, and a paired-change lint: a PR touching RLS on a synced table must also touch the sync-rule test fixtures. Re-run gate named for S6 when EVV tables enter sync scope, and add a planted-canary row scoped to an unassigned client asserted absent from every device bucket.

findings.title: ST-023's required keep-both 'pgTAP lineage check' is unwritable against the schema — form_version has a single-parent pointer, but a merge has two antecedents
findings.detail: ST-023's AC requires 'both antecedents preserved & linked (E2E + pgTAP lineage check)' and Doc 10 §4 says the merge 'outcome saved as a new version; both antecedents preserved and linked.' But Doc 07 §5 form_version carries exactly one lineage column, prev_version_id — a merge version can reference only one parent, so the second antecedent is preserved but not linked, and the promised lineage property test has no invariant to assert. Separately, unique(instance_id, version_no) means two concurrent drafts computing next version_no collide as a raw unique-violation, not the specified 409 → CAREOS_CONFLICT_KEEP_BOTH path (Doc 08 §2) — an interleaving no planned test exercises (E2E 'simulated concurrent edit' drives the row_version path only). The property to test — 'after any interleaving of saves/merges, every version is reachable from the current head via lineage links and no antecedent is orphaned' — must first be made true by the schema.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §5 form_version.prev_version_id, unique(instance_id, version_no); Doc 15 ST-023 AC; Doc 10 §4 conflict UX; Doc 08 §2 CAREOS_CONFLICT_KEEP_BOTH
findings.recommendation: Before S2 (forms sprint): add the second lineage link to Doc 07 §5 (merged_from_version_id uuid, or a form_version_parent link table), then specify the pgTAP lineage property test against it (full-DAG reachability + no orphans on a seeded merge history), plus a concurrency-layer case (per S6-1's harness) for simultaneous version_no assignment asserting the client-visible outcome is the keep-both flow, never a bare unique-violation error.

findings.title: EVV test set has no clock-skew, boundary-geofence, GPS-accuracy, or ungeocoded-client cases — and app.clock_in trusts device time unvalidated
findings.detail: Doc 12 §3 names only 'geofence in/out cases (PostGIS fixtures)'. Missing: (1) clock skew — app.clock_in (Doc 07 §6) writes p_at (device-supplied) as clock_in_at with no comparison against received_at; a phone with a wrong clock (or a manipulated one — EVV times drive Medicaid billing) produces wrong federal Cures-Act time elements submitted to ISAS, silently. No validation exists and no test is named. (2) Boundary cases — point exactly at geofence_radius_m, accuracy_m larger than the radius (a 500m-accuracy fix 'inside' a 150m fence is not evidence of presence), best-of-N sampling behavior (Doc 10 §6). (3) Null geometry — a client not yet geocoded makes st_dwithin return NULL, so v_in is NULL and the CASE routes to 'exception' with within_geofence_in = NULL; plausible-but-unverified behavior that will be common during migration onboarding (every M0/M1 client starts ungeocoded). Offline replay/idempotency is well covered (client_event_id test named; airplane suite at §4) — this finding is only the missing physics.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §6 app.clock_in (p_at, st_dwithin, geofence_radius_m, accuracy columns); Doc 12 §3 RPC guards, §4 mobile suite; Doc 10 §6 EVV capture flow (best-of-N, accuracy shown); Doc 08 §6.1 six federal elements
findings.recommendation: For S6 (EVV sprint): add to the RPC a skew policy (|p_at − now()| > threshold ⇒ flag on visit_event payload and exception-route; never reject — care proceeds) and name pgTAP cases for it; add pgTAP property/fixture cases for at-radius, accuracy>radius, and null-geo; add one Maestro scenario with a skewed device clock; and specify accuracy-vs-radius semantics in Doc 07 §6 so within_geofence_in is a tri-state with documented meaning for the coordinator exception queue.

findings.title: Cadence engine: silent-stop of the pg_cron tick is neither paged nor tested, and the promised time-travel tests need an as-of parameter that Doc 07's function contract doesn't have
findings.detail: The cadence engine is the compliance guarantee ('cadences executed by software'). Its failure mode is silence: if the hourly cron.schedule tick (Doc 07 §7) stops firing, obligations simply stop materializing/transitioning — the dashboard shows fewer overdue items and looks healthier while a 45/90/120-day supervisory visit quietly lapses into a citable deficiency. Doc 13 §6 lists 'cadence-engine tick health' as a dashboard, but Doc 13 §7's page list omits it (pages cover DLQ, WAL, chain-verify, canary — not a stopped tick), and no test anywhere asserts the alert fires when the tick stops (Doc 12 §5's chaos drills are ISAS-down, model-down, restore only). Separately, Doc 12 §3 promises 'time-travel fixtures (clock injection)' for cadence math, but app.evaluate_compliance() as contracted in Doc 07 §7 takes no arguments and the DDL leans on now() defaults — there is no clock to inject, so the promised tests are unimplementable against the current design.
findings.refs: Doc 07 §7 (cron.schedule 'careos_cadence_tick', app.evaluate_compliance()); Doc 13 §6 (dashboard), §7 (page matrix — tick absent); Doc 12 §3 (time-travel fixtures), §5 (chaos drill list); Doc 05/02 via Doc 06 §5.3 (45/90/120 cadences)
findings.recommendation: Two plan edits: (a) Doc 07 §7 — sign app.evaluate_compliance(p_asof timestamptz default now()) so pgTAP can drive DST/leap-year/grace-transition scenarios as Doc 12 §3 intends; (b) Doc 13 §7 — promote cadence-tick staleness to a page via a dead-man switch (tick writes a heartbeat row; alert on age > 2 intervals), and add a named CI/staging test that kills the tick and asserts the alert fires. Add 'cadence-tick down' to the quarterly chaos-drill roster.

findings.title: E3 demo-tenant reset script is an untested destructive path in a product whose premise is that no deletion path exists
findings.detail: E3 (accepted, S0) adds a Meadowbrook 'reset script' so the demo tenant can be restored to a clean state as the 'standing sales stage.' A reset necessarily deletes/truncates tenant rows — including [AO] tables that app.forbid_mutation() and revoked grants exist to protect — so it must run as a privileged owner path, i.e., it is precisely the capability the whole spine forbids, aimed by a tenant_id parameter. The CEO plan does not state which environment the permanent demo tenant lives in (D-006 permits synthetic data anywhere, so staging is possible, but 'permanent... sales stage' suggests prod-adjacent), and specifies no guard or test. A tenant-targeting bug in an owner-privileged reset run where real data lives is a data-loss event. Doc 12 §3's append-only probes ('UPDATE/DELETE as every role incl. a simulated table-owner path raises CAREOS_APPEND_ONLY') were written before a sanctioned owner-level wipe path existed and don't cover it.
findings.refs: CEO plan E3; Doc 12 §3 append-only probes; Doc 07 §1.5/§4 app.forbid_mutation; D-006 (Doc 00 §3); Doc 12 §7 Meadowbrook seed
findings.recommendation: At S0 with ST-006: (a) decide and record the demo tenant's environment (recommend: staging only for Phase 1; a prod demo tenant is its own decision-log entry); (b) add tenant.is_demo (or equivalent flag) and make the reset function hard-fail on any non-demo tenant and on any environment not allowlisted; (c) add pgTAP tests asserting the refusal paths (non-demo tenant, prod env, and that reset of the demo tenant leaves other tenants' row counts untouched); (d) reset runs emit audit events like any consequential action.

findings.title: E5 founder-knowledge capture starts at S1 with free-text answers under an active PHI embargo, and no control or test covers the content
findings.detail: E5 (accepted) writes knowledge_document rows from week 2, with the founder answering 3–5 captured operational questions weekly. The PHI embargo is still on at S1 — Doc 00 §4 requires ALL rows green and V11/V12 verify 'before M0 pilot' — yet a founder answering real operational questions will naturally name real clients and staff ('for Mrs. K we always...'). Free-text real PHI is exactly what the planted-canary suite cannot catch (it detects planted markers, not organic names), and the full canary/minimizer stack doesn't ship until S7 anyway under the resequence. Additionally, while Doc 12 §3's coverage-manifest gate will force generic RLS matrix coverage when the table lands at S1, the knowledge domain's distinctive semantics — scope and sensitivity columns that later gate Brain retrieval (Doc 07 §10: 'RLS on chunks = same predicates as source entities'; Doc 11 §5: sensitive-scope chunks require matching permission) — have no named tests, and six sprints of captured content will hit the embedder at S7 with whatever scoping it accumulated.
findings.refs: CEO plan E5; Doc 00 §4 (V11/V12 'before M0 pilot'; 'nothing PHI until every row green'); Doc 07 §10 knowledge tables; Doc 11 §5 (sensitivity gating); Doc 12 §6 (canary = planted markers only); design doc S7 (canary suite lands S7)
findings.recommendation: Add to the E5 story: (a) an embargo-period content control — capture UI instructs de-identification, and each answer passes a review step (the RN SME or Salim) before commit, recorded on the row; (b) named pgTAP tests for knowledge_document/knowledge_chunk scope+sensitivity predicates at S1, not S7; (c) an S7 pre-embedding gate: a one-time sweep of accumulated capture rows for identifiers before the corpus is embedded, logged as migration-style evidence. Cheap now, unfixable after six sprints of accumulation.

findings.title: Compliance-evidence outputs (E1 survey packet, migration scorecard, exec compliance heat) are tested as journeys, never against a COMAR ground-truth oracle
findings.detail: Three features exist to make claims to a surveyor or the founder about compliance completeness, and none has a correctness test — only 'the flow runs' coverage. (1) E1 app.export_survey_packet moves to S4 and becomes the founder's sharpest moment; Doc 12 §4 lists 'survey-packet export' as an E2E journey, but no test asserts the packet contains every required evidence class for a client/range — a packet silently missing a consent or a supervisory-visit note is worse than no packet, because it's trusted.
